together.settings.page.title: Together · Co-op Mode
together.settings.section.title: Co-op Mode
together.settings.enabled.label: Enable co-op mode (shared deck)
together.settings.enabled.on: Currently: on — the character-select screen shows a "Join Co-op Mode" button; 2+ players joining then share one body.
together.settings.enabled.off: Currently: off — this mod stays out of your runs entirely.
together.settings.merge.label: Merge starting decks (shared deck = p1 + p2)
together.settings.merge.description:
On: when a run starts, the other player's (echo / p2) starting deck is copied into the shared deck, so the group plays both players' starting cards together.
Off: the shared deck only holds the anchor's (p1, the one who joined first) starting deck; the echo's deck is left out.
Note: it is a copy, so if both players pick the same character you get two starting decks (two Silent = 24 cards). Turn it off to keep just one.
together.settings.hp.label: Max HP bonus: percent of p2's max HP (0~100)
together.settings.hp.description:
How much of the echo's (p2) max HP is added to the shared HP pool: 0 = none, 100 = all of it.
Applied once, when a new run starts (the new max is written into the save, so loading or reconnecting never adds it again).
Integers 0~100 only; anything else is ignored and the previous value is kept.
together.settings.gold.label: Shared gold (one wallet for the group)
together.settings.gold.description:
On: every member shares one gold balance — whoever picks gold up or spends it in a shop changes the same wallet.
A new run adds everyone's starting gold together (99 × members; only once per run, loading or reconnecting never adds it again). Off: everyone keeps their own gold.
In multiplayer the host's setting wins.
together.settings.compat.title: Compatibility (high-risk patches)
together.settings.compat.order.label: Total order for card ordering (CardModel.CompareTo)
together.settings.compat.order.descripti:
On: cards get a deterministic total order so both ends sort/shuffle identically.
Off: vanilla comparer — order may drift between the two ends (only turn this off if another mod conflicts).
together.settings.compat.dedupe.label: Hook listener de-duplication
together.settings.compat.dedupe.descript:
On: when a shared pile/deck makes the same card show up twice, listeners are de-duplicated by reference.
Off: vanilla behaviour (a duplicated listener may fire twice, e.g. auto-play powers).
together.settings.compat.widen.label: Relic hook 「group-wide」 dispatch
together.settings.compat.widen.descripti:
On: in a co-op run, the 「card entered deck」 notification is dispatched once per member — relics that claim cards by owner (e.g. Book of Five Rings) then count for the whole group.
Off: vanilla behaviour (only the card's owner is notified). Both ends stay consistent either way; the echo's copy just stops counting.
together.settings.compat.cardview.label: Blank the echo's shared-card view
together.settings.compat.cardview.descri:
On: during monster moves the echo's shared-card view returns empty, so a shared batch of cards is processed once.
Off: everyone sees them (a monster move that iterates shared cards may process them twice).
together.settings.compat.echopopulate.la: Echo does not re-fill the combat piles
together.settings.compat.echopopulate.de:
On: on entering combat only the anchor copies the master deck into the draw pile — there is one master deck, so the echo filling it again would double the deck.
Off: the echo fills its piles as well (the shared deck becomes two copies). Only turn this off when another mod takes over the echo's combat piles itself.
together.settings.orbcap.label: Shared orb slot cap
together.settings.orbcap.description:
Members share one orb queue, so its capacity is scaled by this rule.
Auto: 10 × members that actually have orb slots (two Defects = 20; a single one keeps 10) — default.
Vanilla 10: exactly like the base game; slots run out fast when shared.
10 × every member: ignores the character (a 3-player run with one Defect still gets 30).
In multiplayer the host's setting wins.
together.settings.compat.mirroredpower.l: Mirrored powers tick down once per turn end
together.settings.compat.mirroredpower.d:
On: the six body-stat turn-end powers (temporary Strength/Dexterity/Focus, Weak/Vulnerable/Frail) are settled only by the original copy, not by each mirror.
Off: every mirror settles too (values double up or go negative).
together.settings.compat.imbued.label: Imbued auto-plays once per combat
together.settings.compat.imbued.descript:
On: the same Imbued card auto-plays only once per combat (deduplicated by object reference).
Off: vanilla per-player dispatch (Imbued may auto-play twice; the second one often stalls in a choice screen).
On: with Random Foreseer installed, each prediction builds a single copy of the shared draw pile / orb queue — fixes "draw prediction keeps showing the same first card" and inaccurate orb damage forecasts.
Off: their prediction core is left completely alone (forecasts fall back to its original algorithm).
Has no effect when that mod is not installed.
together.settings.compat.note:
This group is on by default. These patches touch paths the base game itself uses, so switch them off one by one only when another mod conflicts.
In multiplayer the host's settings win (otherwise one side on / one side off would desync).
together.settings.diag.title: Diagnostics / feedback
together.settings.diag.export.label: Export current environment (mod list / settings / session)
together.settings.diag.export.descriptio:
Writes "enabled mod list + effective settings + current session state" as a txt into the game's log folder (next to godot.log): together-modlist.txt.
The folder opens automatically afterwards. When reporting a bug, send that file together with godot.log.
This button works from the in-combat pause screen too (the other settings rows are read-only during a run).
together.settings.diag.note: Everything is read through public APIs (the game's mod load order + RitsuLib's mod inventory), and the same text is also written to the log with a [together][env] prefix — so a log-only report still carries it.
together.settings.diag.test.label: Test the alert popup (verifies export + popup end to end)
together.settings.diag.test.description:
Clicking it will: (1) build a feedback bundle right away (environment snapshot + a copy of godot.log); (2) show exactly the same popup a real bug would show; (3) the popup's "Open folder" button jumps to that bundle folder.
If another modal (e.g. the divergence panel) is open right now, it only exports and skips the popup — same behaviour as a real alert.
together.settings.diag.alertpopup.label: Popup when a self-check fails (this machine only)
together.settings.diag.alertpopup.descri:
On (default): when a desync / one of our own assertions / a failed patch class is detected, show a popup telling you which two files to send.
Off: no popup — the feedback bundle is still built automatically and the log still gets the "⚠ 自检异常（…）｜反馈包：…" line; you just won't be interrupted.
This is a per-machine preference (never synced from the host): turning it off on the host does not silence a client and vice versa.
